title: Orphan nuclear receptors: structural mechanisms, ligand discovery, and therapeutic potential.
authors: Liu, Yunlong; Wei, Shirong; Wang, Ziheng; Yang, Helian; Chen, Zhongzhou; Ren, Mengtian; Fu, Xiuping
one_liner_zh: 综述孤儿核受体的配体识别结构机制与配体发现策略，涉及核受体-DNA互作的结构基础，但非聚焦TF-DNA结合建模，方法上仅提及虚拟筛选与MD模拟，深度有限。
abstract: Orphan nuclear receptors (ONRs) are members of the nuclear receptor superfamily initially identified without clearly defined endogenous high-affinity ligands. Nevertheless, increasing evidence demonstrates that they play essential roles in regulating metabolism, development, neural function, and tumorigenesis. Recent advances in structural biology, chemical biology, and systems biology have improved understanding of ligand recognition and regulatory mechanisms in these receptors. This review summarizes current progress in ONRs ligand research. ONRs are categorized according to their physiological roles in metabolic homeostasis, development and reproduction, and neuro-immune and cancer-related regulation, highlighting their involvement in diseases such as metabolic disorders, cancers, neurological diseases, and reproductive abnormalities. We discuss the structural basis of ligand recognition, focusing on conserved features of the ligand-binding domain (LBD) and structural variations, particularly in the alpha10 and AF-2 helices, that influence ligand accessibility and transcriptional regulation. Structural studies have revealed ligand-receptor complexes for representative ONRs, including ROR, HNF-4, REV-ERB, ERR, SF-1, and LRH-1, identifying ligand types such as lipids, heme, and phospholipids. In contrast, other receptors, including TR4, DAX-1, COUP-TFII, and Nur77, currently have only functional evidence supporting potential ligand interactions. Key strategies for ligand discovery include endogenous ligand co-purification, phenotype-based high-throughput screening, structural biology approaches, and structure-based virtual screening combined with molecular dynamics simulations. Major challenges include difficulties in endogenous ligand identification, context-dependent regulation, and limitations in achieving receptor subtype selectivity in drug development. Future progress will rely on integrating structural, biochemical, and multi-omics approaches to facilitate therapeutic targeting of ONRs.
abstract_zh: 孤儿核受体（Orphan nuclear receptors, ONRs）是核受体超家族的成员，最初被发现时其内源性高亲和力配体尚未明确。然而，越来越多的证据表明，它们在调节代谢、发育、神经功能和肿瘤发生中发挥重要作用。结构生物学、化学生物学和系统生物学的最新进展增进了对这些受体中配体识别和调控机制的理解。本综述总结了ONRs配体研究的当前进展。根据ONRs在代谢稳态、发育与生殖以及神经免疫和癌症相关调控中的生理作用对其进行分类，重点突出它们在代谢性疾病、癌症、神经系统疾病和生殖异常等疾病中的参与。我们讨论了配体识别的结构基础，聚焦于配体结合域（ligand-binding domain, LBD）的保守特征和结构变异，特别是alpha10和AF-2螺旋中的变异，这些变异影响配体可及性和转录调控。结构研究已揭示了代表性ONRs的配体-受体复合物，包括ROR、HNF-4、REV-ERB、ERR、SF-1和LRH-1，并鉴定了脂质、血红素和磷脂等配体类型。相比之下，其他受体，包括TR4、DAX-1、COUP-TFII和Nur77，目前仅有功能证据支持潜在的配体相互作用。配体发现的关键策略包括内源性配体共纯化、基于表型的高通量筛选、结构生物学方法以及基于结构的虚拟筛选结合分子动力学模拟。主要挑战包括内源性配体鉴定的困难、背景依赖性调控以及药物开发中实现受体亚型选择性的局限性。未来进展将依赖于整合结构、生化和多组学方法，以促进ONRs的治疗靶向。
